description: Chivalric romance. Knights, stewards and chaplains; oaths and obligation rather than coin.

appearance.squire: Sixteen, cold, and holding somebody else's helm as if it were an egg.
appearance.armourer: Burn-marked to the elbow, and squinting at a rivet you cannot see.
appearance.porter: Filling the gateway on purpose, with a staff he has not needed yet.
appearance.chaplain: Ink to the knuckle, and a cloak worn thin across the shoulders.
appearance.harper: Fingers wrapped against the cold, tuning something that is already in tune.
appearance.pilgrim: Mud to the thigh, a badge of tin, and the look of somebody counting days.
appearance.ferryman: Standing in the boat rather than beside it, out of long habit.
appearance.fowler: Nets over one shoulder, and three birds hanging from a cord.
appearance.hermit: Barefoot in this weather, which he does not appear to have noticed.
appearance.bondsman: Working, and not stopping while you talk.
appearance.widow: Neat, grey and composed, with black worn well past the mourning.
appearance.child: Small, unbothered, and staring at your axe.
appearance.groom: Smells of horse and wet straw. Speaks to you as if you were one.
appearance.steward: A tally-stick in each hand and no patience in either.
appearance.netmaker: Mending, with the work hooked over one bare toe.

talksAbout.squire: who is riding out, and who is quietly not
talksAbout.armourer: what a green axe is worth as metal, which is nothing
talksAbout.porter: who has been let in this winter, which is very few
talksAbout.chaplain: the year turning, and the vow that turns with it
talksAbout.harper: the verses about the Green Knight, which he has been asked not to sing
talksAbout.pilgrim: the road north, and how much of it is under water
talksAbout.ferryman: the channel, the tide, and what the fen has swallowed lately
talksAbout.fowler: the birds going over early, and what that means for the frost
talksAbout.hermit: a chapel out in the dale that nobody has consecrated
talksAbout.steward: the stores, the winter, and the hunting that will not fill either

lore.title: A Blow for a Blow
lore.premise: A green man rode into the hall at New Year, let a knight take his head off, picked it up and asked for the return blow in a year. The year is up.
lore.era: the turning of the year, and the twelfth winter of the Round Table

ambient: The frost has not come off the north side of anything today.
Somewhere behind you a bird goes up out of the reeds, and nothing follows it.
Your breath is going ahead of you in the cold.
There is holly in the hedge, and a great deal of it.
The track has been ridden this winter, but not lately.
